newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK CBANK SAYS SEES NO DEVAL, RESERVES STRONG.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK CBANK SAYS SEES NO DEVAL, RESERVES STRONG.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) sees no reason to devalue the crown in the foreseeable future, a senior NBS official said on Thursday.

"We will not consider crown devaluation in the foreseeable future, as we have sufficient hard currency reserves currently covering about 3.6 months of imports," NBS Vice-governor Marian Jusko told journalists at a finance conference in Bratislava.
NBS hard currency reserves totalled $3.5 billion as of November 20, compared with some $3.05 billion in November 1995.

Jusko added that from a long-term perspective, maintaining a stable crown will not be possible without improvement of the country's exports, economic competitiveness and a functioning industrial policy.
"If somebody says it is possible (to maintain stable currency) over a period of, let's say, 10 years, without these factors, he would not know what he is talking about," Jusko said.
